question: Assume today is 2026-10-16. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of live births in South Korea in August 2026, as it will be first reported in the national statistics agency's monthly Population Trends release.

target.what: Number of live births in South Korea during August 2026, as first reported in the national statistics agency's monthly Population Trends release (population trend / vital statistics).
target.cadence: monthly, with a lag of roughly 2–3 months after the reference month
target.caveats: Working interpretation: registered live births occurring in August 2026, by month of occurrence, as published in the provisional monthly vital statistics. Alternative definitions that could materially change the answer include: (a) births by month of registration rather than month of occurrence; (b)

candidates.perspective: Statistics Korea monthly vital statistics time series
candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 live births can be projected from the same month in prior years, adjusted for the recent trend and any known calendar effects. The target is a monthly flow with strong seasonality and a declining trend.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly live births for South Korea from January 2023 through July 2026 (or the latest available month before the cutoff), with August values for 2023, 2024, and 2025. Minimum evidence: the most recent 12–24 monthly observations and the August values for the last three years.
search_hints: KOSTAT population trends live births August

candidates.perspective: Marriage and birth registration administrative data
candidates.hypothesis: Live births are strongly linked to the number of marriages in prior periods, with a typical lag of 1–3 years. A change in marriages can signal a change in births, though the relationship is weakening.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly marriage registrations in South Korea for 2023–2026, and if possible the ratio of births to marriages at relevant lags. Minimum evidence: monthly marriage counts for the last 36 months and a historical births-to-marriages ratio.

candidates.perspective: Population and women of childbearing age
candidates.hypothesis: Births equal the number of women of childbearing age multiplied by the general fertility rate. Changes in the size and age structure of this population, combined with fertility intentions, drive the level of births.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly or quarterly estimates of the female population aged 15–49 in South Korea for 2025–2026, and recent general fertility rates or age-specific fertility rates. Minimum evidence: the latest population estimates by age and sex and a recent fertility rate.

candidates.perspective: Policy and economic shocks affecting births
candidates.hypothesis: Government pronatalist policies, housing costs, and economic conditions can shift birth timing and numbers. Any major policy introduced in 2025–2026 could affect August 2026 births.
candidates.data_to_find: Announcements of new birth incentives, parental leave expansions, or housing support in South Korea during 2025–2026, and any evidence of their take-up or impact on birth intentions. Minimum evidence: a list of major policy changes and expert assessments of their likely effect.

candidates.hypothesis: Statistics Korea or other institutions may publish monthly or quarterly birth projections or nowcasts that can serve as a direct estimate for August 2026.
candidates.data_to_find: Any published forecast or nowcast of South Korean monthly live births for 2026, especially for August 2026, from KOSTAT, Bank of Korea, or research institutes. Minimum evidence: a numerical projection for the target month or quarter.

candidates.perspective: Birth registration data from local governments
candidates.hypothesis: Some local governments or the Ministry of the Interior and Safety may publish monthly birth registration counts earlier than KOSTAT. These can be used as a leading indicator for the national figure.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly birth registration counts from the Ministry of the Interior and Safety (행정안전부) or provincial governments for 2026, especially August 2026. Minimum evidence: a national or large-sample monthly count for August 2026.

candidates.hypothesis: August births have a consistent seasonal pattern relative to the annual total or to adjacent months. A seasonal index can be applied to a known annual or year-to-date total to estimate August.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly seasonal factors for South Korean births (e.g., August as a percentage of annual births) from recent years. Minimum evidence: the August share of annual births for 2023, 2024, and 2025.
search_hints: South Korea birth seasonality monthly pattern

candidates.perspective: Neighboring countries with similar demographic trends
candidates.hypothesis: Countries like Japan or Taiwan may have already reported August 2026 births, and their year-on-year changes could provide a rough signal for South Korea, given shared regional trends.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly live births for Japan and Taiwan for August 2026 (or the latest available months), and their year-on-year changes. Minimum evidence: August 2026 or recent monthly birth counts for at least one comparable country.

assessment.note: Same KOSTAT August 2025 release: level 20,867 and +3.8% YoY are internally consistent (implies Aug 2024 ≈ 20,103). p1 is the anchor level for the August seasonal route.
All describe the same July 2026 KOSTAT release (24,275; +11.1%; +2,421). Multiple URLs, one underlying measurement — counts as one observation, not five.
Same Jan–Jul 2026 cumulative +14.7% (17만79명, +21,851). One measurement, two outlets.
July 2026 TFR 0.89, +0.08 — same KOSTAT release repeated. Useful as a level check on the birth surge, not as an independent estimate.
June 2026: 23,111, +3,115, +15.6% — same release, three outlets. June is the last month with a confirmed level before the target.
June 2026 TFR 0.88, +0.11 — same release.

Monthly YoY growth path in 2026: Jan +11.7, Feb +13.6, Mar +19.4, Apr +18.0, May +13.6, Jun +15.6, Jul +11.1. Consistent decelerating-but-still-double-digit regime; these are the key inputs for a YoY-transfer route.
Q2 2026 +15.8% and H1 2026 +15.4% — same underlying registration data, consistent with the monthly path.
2024 monthly shares of annual births sum to ~100% and give August = 8.4%. Internally consistent seasonal profile for a recent year.
1981–2023 cumulative shares give August = 8.0%. Older but long-run; the two seasonal vintages (8.0% vs 8.4%) bracket the August share and are not contradictory.

p1.role: South Korea live births in August 2025 (persons), the base level for the same calendar month one year earlier

a1.role: ratio of August 2026 live births to August 2025 live births, i.e. the one-year growth factor for the target month

methods.rationale: Primary route: carry the observed August 2025 level (p1 = 20,867) forward by the 2026 YoY growth factor. The growth factor is anchored on the observed 2026 monthly path (p60, p61, p95, p96, p97, p44, p10/p11) and the Jan–Jul cumulative +14.7% (p20), with the assumption a1 supplying the August-specific value. Shared dependency: p1 and the 2026 monthly growth observations come from the same KOSTAT registration system, so a systematic revision to 2026 registrations would move both. Main failure mode: the 2026 surge decelerating faster than assumed, or August 2025 being revised.

p10.role: South Korea live births in July 2026 (persons), used as the most recent observed monthly level

a2.role: August share of 2026 annual live births (percent), the seasonal coefficient converting a monthly level to the August level

methods.rationale: Cross-check route using the seasonal structure: scale the most recent observed monthly level (July 2026, p10 = 24,275) by the ratio of August's annual share to July's annual share. July's 2024 share was 8.6% (p76) and August's 8.4% (p73), so August is slightly below July; a2 encodes the August share and the July share is embedded in the observed July level. This route is independent of the YoY-growth assumption but shares the KOSTAT registration source with m1. Main failure mode: the July-to-August seasonal ratio drifting, or July 2026 being an unusually high base.

Naive seasonal benchmark: use the same month one year earlier (August 2025 = 20,867, p1) as the estimate. This is the no-change baseline against which the 2026 growth routes are judged; it is deliberately conservative and will be down-weighted by backtesting if the 2026 surge persists, but it guards against over-extrapolating a single year's rebound.

assumptions.name: August 2026 YoY growth factor applied to August 2025 live births
assumptions.rationale: The 2026 monthly YoY growth path is Jan +11.7%, Feb +13.6%, Mar +19.4%, Apr +18.0%, May +13.6%, Jun +15.6%, Jul +11.1% (p60, p61, p96, p97, p95, p44, p10/p11), with cumulative Jan–Jul +14.7% (p20). assumptions.falsified_by: A published August 2026 registration count or KOSTAT release showing YoY growth outside roughly +4% to +19%, or evidence that the 2026 surge reversed sharply after July.

p1.role: South Korea live births in August 2025 (month of occurrence), the base level for the same calendar month one year earlier

a1.role: ratio of August 2026 live births to August 2025 live births, i.e. the YoY growth factor for the target month

methods.rationale: Direct YoY transfer: August 2025 KOSTAT live births (20,867) times an assumed August 2026 growth factor. The growth factor is anchored on the observed 2026 monthly path (July +11.1%, June +15.6%, May +13.6%, cumulative Jan–Jul +14.7%) and on the fact that August 2025 was a strong base. Shared dependency: both the base and the growth factor come from the same KOSTAT vital-statistics system, so a definitional change would move both. Main failure mode: the 2026 spring surge could be a timing shift that reverses in August, making the assumed growth factor too high.

p56.role: South Korea total live births in calendar year 2025, used as the base annual total for the seasonal-share route

a2.role: August share of annual live births, expressed as a fraction of the annual total

methods.rationale: Seasonal-share route: 2025 annual births (254,457) times the August share of annual births. The share is anchored on the 2024 August share (8.4%, p73) and the 1981–2023 cumulative share (8.0%, p85). This route is independent of the YoY-growth route in its main uncertainty (seasonality rather than the 2026 growth rate), but it shares the KOSTAT annual-total base. Main failure mode: the 2026 annual total is not yet known, so using 2025 as the base implicitly assumes 2026 annual births are near 2025; if 2026 births are running ~15% above 2025, this route will understate August unless the share is adjusted upward.

YoY scaling using the target's own August history and the July 2026 live-birth level as the signal. The signal must have a value for the target's year and the year before; July 2026 (24,275) and July 2025 are both available from the same KOSTAT release, so the method scales August 2025 by the July 2026/July 2025 ratio. Shared dependency: both series come from the same monthly vital-statistics release, so a revision to the July figure would move the estimate. Main failure mode: July and August have different seasonal positions and different 2025 base strengths, so the July YoY ratio is an imperfect proxy for the August YoY ratio.

Naive seasonal benchmark: the most recent observed August value (August 2025, 20,867) as a no-change forecast. This is a deliberately conservative anchor that ignores the 2026 upturn; it is included as a lower-bound-style benchmark rather than a central expectation, and its historical error will be large in a year with a strong trend.

assumptions.name: August 2026 YoY growth factor for Korean live births
assumptions.rationale: The 2026 monthly YoY growth path decelerated from +19.4% (March) and +18.0% (April) to +13.6% (May), +15.6% (June) and +11.1% (July), while the Jan–Jul cumulative was +14.7%. August 2025 was itself a strong base (+3.8%), so a further step down toward the low double digits is plausible; the range spans roughly +4% to +16% to reflect the possibility that the spring surge fades faster or holds.
assumptions.applies_when: The August 2026 KOSTAT provisional release follows the same month-of-occurrence definition and the recent deceleration continues; it transfers to the target month because August 2026 is the next month after the observed July 2026 figure.
